Nina: Heads-up — HorizonHealth disputed INV-2026-11-18. They were billed burst fees after a model quantization rollout; they believe some requests were double-counted. Asking for refund + SLA credit.

Paul: assigning to @chelsea for usage recon. Can you pull meter logs for 2026-11-18 14:20-14:45 UTC? Customer says traffic should have stayed on horizon-ded-2.

Chelsea: checking logs now. early finding: during the quantization rollout we had a brief overlap where both old and new model variants were tagged for the same request stream. That produced duplicate meter entries for ~13 minutes.

Chelsea: quick snippet: pool_hits:
2026-11-18T14:22Z -> horizon-ded-2
2026-11-18T14:22Z -> horizon-ded-2-quantized
Estimated overcharge = $13,250.

Finance-bot: Policy: cash refunds > $5k require director + legal approval. SLA credits <=15% can be applied automatically; manual approvals allowed for larger goodwill credits.

Nina: HorizonHealth is a multi-year customer; recommend refund the exact overcharge and apply a 7% SLA credit to next invoice. Need sam + legal.

Paul: charge ids: CHG-16233, CHG-16234. Recon worksheet in ticket #4710 with per-minute breakdown and the rollout plan. Root cause: overlap in variant tagging during canary > prod promotion.

Legal-bot: Contract SOW permits "credit or refund" for failure to honor reserved capacity. Recommend amendment note documenting refund and mitigation.

Sam: Approved for refund and 7% SLA credit. Please process refund and include remediation summary in the customer message.

Chelsea: engineering note — we'll update the rollout script to atomically swap tags and add a post-promotion audit. ETA patch: 24h.

Nina: Action items: 1) run refund `/process-refund CHG-16233,CHG-16234 amount=13250 ticket=4710 note="HorizonHealth - duplicate metering during quantization rollout"`, 2) apply 7% SLA credit, 3) send customer communication with logs and mitigation.

Paul: I'll run the command and send the note. Closing ticket #4710 after refund posts.
